items.title: The day I failed my driving test
items.body: I failed my driving test twice. My father told me to slow down and never give up. The third time I passed, and I learned that patience beats panic.

items.title: Honesty
items.body: Tell the truth, even when it costs you. A lie saves you a minute and costs you years.

items.title: How I learned to save money
items.body: My grandmother made me save a tenth of every pay cheque before I spent anything. I still do it, and it carried us through hard times.

items.title: Meeting your mother
items.body: I met your mother at a church fete in 1994. She laughed at my terrible jokes, and I knew I wanted to marry her.

items.title: Work
items.body: Work hard, but never let work become more important than the people you love. Rest on Sundays.

items.title: When I was afraid
items.body: When I lost my job in 2008 I was afraid for the first time as a father. I prayed, I asked friends for help, and I found new work within four months.

items.title: Friends
items.body: Choose friends who tell you the truth, not friends who only tell you what you want to hear.

items.title: Sunday breyani
items.body: Every Sunday I cooked breyani with your aunt. The secret is patience: let the rice steam slowly and never lift the lid.

items.title: My school days
items.body: I was not a good student until standard eight, when Mr Naidoo showed me that mathematics was a puzzle. After that I studied every night.

items.title: Faith
items.body: Faith for me was never about rules. It was about gratitude, and about looking after people who have less.

items.title: The worst argument with my brother
items.body: My brother and I did not speak for two years after an argument about money. I regret it. Apologise first, even when you think you are right.

items.title: Our trip to the Drakensberg
items.body: We hiked to the Amphitheatre in 2012. You were six and complained the whole way, then refused to leave the top.

items.title: Looking after your body
items.body: Walk every day, sleep enough, and go to the doctor before small problems become big ones.

items.title: The year we lost the house
items.body: In 2009 we lost the house and moved in with your grandparents. We were poor for a while but we were together.

items.title: Learning the guitar
items.body: I taught myself the guitar at forty from library books. It is never too late to learn something new.

items.title: Kindness to strangers
items.body: Be kind to people who can do nothing for you. That is how you know who you really are.

items.title: Secret family recipe
items.body: The secret ingredient is cinnamon and a pinch of nutmeg.

items.title: Politics
items.body: DRAFT: my views on elections are not settled yet.

items.title: Voice note about weekends
items.body: Weekends were for family and long breakfasts.
